display.purpose: The hero promise and route headlines. Weight 400, left-set, never bold.

lede.purpose: Every section h2, written as a two-tone sentence pair with <b> on the lead clause.

eyebrow.purpose: Instrument Serif italic on section eyebrows and feature indices — the asides a person wrote.

action.purpose: Instrument Serif on button labels, both variants, since they always appear as a pair.

figure.purpose: Instrument Serif on the stat-band numerals.

label.purpose: Geist Mono uppercase for engine output only: citations, source paths, token counts, statuses, commands.

elevation.note: No drop shadows anywhere. Depth is carried entirely by the neutral tonal ramp (#000 through #18191B) and 1px hairline borders. The only box-shadows in the system are accent halo rings on status dots and an inset 1px selection ring, neither of which is elevation.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for every state transition and panel entrance.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, and selection changes on controls.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Accordion content, menu entrance, and fact insertion.

motion.name: field-drift
motion.purpose: Horizontal drift of the hero bar field; slow enough to read as ambient rather than animated.

motion.name: ambient-drift
motion.purpose: Drift of the page-wide ambient wash below the hero.

motion.name: type-cadence
motion.purpose: Hero clause typing; disabled entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Single-column primitives, stacked hero actions, one-line announcement bar.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Feature showcases, compatibility, privacy, and FAQ collapse to one column.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Desktop nav and header chips give way to the sheet menu.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Scroll-spy rail flips from a sticky column to a horizontal strip.

breakpoints.name: short-viewport
breakpoints.purpose: Hero type and padding trim so both actions stay above the fold.

breakpoints.name: very-short-viewport
breakpoints.purpose: Hero subheading is dropped; headline scales down further.

ambientField.rule: A fixed, full-viewport WebGL wash sits behind every section except the hero.
ambientField.note: Slow fbm luminance clouds with a faint accent tint and a whisper of vertical striation. Median near 9/255 over black, peak near 17/255, floor near 3/255 so no region stays pure black — deliberately below surface-bright (27/255) so panels keep their edge. Requires precision highp float (mediump is fp16 on many desktop GPUs and quantises a ramp this shallow), a half-level output dither for 8-bit panels, and any periodic term keyed to CSS pixels rather than the backing buffer. Rendered at devicePixelRatio 1 since it carries no fine detail, paused while the document is hidden, and not mounted at all under prefers-reduced-motion. The hero paints an opaque black ground so the two fields never overlap.

surfaceFill.rule: The landing hero is min-height: min(calc(100svh - var(--header-height) - var(--announce-height)), var(--hero-max)), where --hero-max is 50rem.
surfaceFill.note: Below the cap the hero fills the viewport; past it the hero stops at 50rem so the primitives row comes into view and the headline holds the same absolute position it has on a laptop. Physical screen size is not exposed by any web API, so viewport height is the proxy — and it also responds to a resized window. The WebGL bar field fills that box exactly at any screen size. Column count derives from the measured CSS width at roughly one bar per 13px (clamped 40-300), so density is constant from a 375px phone to a 3440px ultrawide rather than scaling with aspect ratio. devicePixelRatio is clamped to 1.5 and re-read on display change.

components.name: Typed Hero Clause
components.description: Signature component. The stem is fixed; only the clause below types and cycles. The clause is a block so it owns its own row and the stem can never reflow, and it reserves its own height. Decorative: aria-hidden, with a stable phrase alongside for assistive technology, and no caret under reduced motion.
components.html: AI familiar with your work without handing over the archive.without handing over the archive.
components.css: .ds-hero-h1 { margin: 0; max-width: 17em; color: #FFFFFF; font: 400 clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4.25rem)/1.125 Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.04em; text-wrap: pretty; } .ds-typed { display: block; min-height: 1.125em; color: #797D86; } .ds-caret { display: inline-block; width: .06em; height: .78em; margin-left: .06em; translate: 0 .06em; background: #FFFFFF; animation: ds-caret-blink 1.05s steps(1, end) infinite; } .ds-sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; } @keyframes ds-caret-blink { 0%, 50% { opacity: 1; } 50.01%, 100% { opacity: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-caret { display: none; } }

narrative.overview: The site reads as instrumentation on a black field: pure black ground, hairline rules, flat tonal panels, and a single rare teal-green that marks live state. Structure comes from alignment and type scale rather than from cards, glow, or tinted glass. The reference is Neon's developer-infrastructure language — left-set headlines, two-tone paragraph headings, a full-bleed generative hero field, and monospace micro-labels — carrying Othie's own document-to-context mechanism.
keyCharacteristics: Pure black canvas with flat, near-neutral panels; no tinted or frosted surfaces
Left-aligned display type at weight 400, never bold, tracked tight at -0.04em
Two-tone paragraph headings: the lead clause in white, its continuation in muted grey
A generative field of vertical light bars filling the first viewport, fading to black
Small radii (4–6px) everywhere except pills on buttons and status chips

rules.name: The Rare Signal Rule
rules.body: The signal (#47E1BD) is never a surface and never a button. It marks live state, selected sources, citation lines, the active rail item, and a small minority of columns in the hero field — roughly two to five percent of a viewport. It sits deliberately brighter and more teal than the reference's green so the signal reads as Othie's own.

rules.name: The White Action Rule
rules.body: The primary button is white on black with near-black text. Secondary actions are a 1px hairline pill. Colour is not used to indicate primacy.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Heading Rule
rules.body: Section headings are written as a sentence pair. The first clause is wrapped in <b> and renders white at weight 400; the remainder inherits --heading-muted. This is the site's primary typographic signature — use it for every h2.

rules.name: The Stable Headline Rule
rules.body: Headlines do not type, flicker, or cycle. The mechanism moves around a stable value proposition.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Constrain display headings with rem, never ch. A ch measure set on a wrapper resolves against the wrapper's 1rem font size and collapses the heading into a narrow column.

dos: Do write every section heading as a two-tone sentence pair with <b> on the lead clause.
Do show Othie's mechanism through clearly labeled illustrative source and citation data.
Do bind every brand treatment, including canvas/WebGL colour, to the central accent token.
Do let hairlines, alignment, and quiet space carry the structure.
donts: Don't centre body sections or use a teal-tinted near-black ground.
Don't make the primary button the accent colour, or use the accent as a panel fill.
Don't set display weights above 400, or use gradient text and pervasive glow.
Don't turn the page into a grid of generic feature cards.
Don't imply an illustrative UI, installer, integration, or price already ships.
